note: Quick, Draw! cell phone 6131839389401088, a brick cordless handset seen from the front. Stroke 0 is the outline of the body, stroke 1 the line under the earpiece, strokes 2 and 3 small marks on the earpiece, strokes 4 to 8 the screen and the keypad buttons, stroke 9 the line above the base, stroke 10 the round button in the base, stroke 11 the antenna on the top left. The phone in the film is rigid: it floats, turns from a diagonal toward upright and gets smaller. The rig places the whole drawing by two points, the middle of the top edge and the middle of the bottom edge, so it turns and shrinks with the phone; no part bends. The drawing is placed by those two points and sized across by a _scale entry in each key, so it is about 1.35 times as wide as the real handset and stretched about 1.5 times along its length: the doodle is a squat phone and the film's handset is a long brick, and this keeps most of the doodle's proportions while its ends sit on the handset's ends. Keys were measured from the SAM outline's long axis (the end where it is at least half its full width, so the antenna is not counted) and shifted by eye onto the handset's centre line.
